body:
chrome.permissions.request opens Chrome's own confirmation dialog and REQUIRES a human click; it also must be called straight from a click handler in an extension page (the MV3 service worker can never supply a user gesture).

Consequence for automation: a headless CDP driver that calls it HANGS INDEFINITELY — no error, no timeout, just a silent stall. CDP's Runtime.evaluate userGesture:true satisfies the gesture requirement but does NOT dismiss the dialog.

Workaround for an e2e: pre-grant the origin by adding it to the BUILT manifest's host_permissions before launching (never the source manifest), and say at the point of use why. Observed on Chrome 154.0.8037.93, 2026-10-02.
